messages:
alice: Quick follow-up from RFC review: we need a proven dry-run path for region handoffs that respects data-residency rules. Main ask: operators want visibility without creating risk of accidental data egress.

ben: Agreed. The naive prewarm caused a EU->NA priming incident in staging last week. We need guardrails so priming can run, but secrets and live payloads never leave origin region.

priya: Suggestion: split "priming" into (1) metadata/schema priming and (2) secret-backed hydration. Dry-run should only perform (1) and produce a report listing which objects would require secret hydration.

marco: We can implement a "dry-token" that authorizes metadata priming. Dry-token must be read-only, single-use for audit, and loggable. No KMS access allowed with dry-token.

dana: UX: operator clicks "prepare handoff (dry run)" -> system returns a matrix: datasets + flags (needs-secret, size, estimated-time). That matrix should be downloadable as CSV.

alice: Good. Also we need a policy layer: some tenants have residency=required (never allow secret hydration outside region). That should block commit until operator explicitly approves and the tenant's compliance contact signs off.

ben: How to enforce at data plane? My idea: data plane accepts only two header combos: metadata-priming with X-Dry-Token, and commit-priming with X-Prewarm-Token + X-Consent-Assertion. Anything else rejected.

priya: Consent assertion can't be freeform. It must map to a consent record produced by control-plane. Example: X-Consent-Assertion: consent_id=cons_9876;signature=sha256(...). Auth-service verifies consent against lease.

marco: Token lifecycle: dry-token TTL 5m, prewarm-token default TTL 10m. Both tokens single-lease, single-region. Add revocation endpoint: POST /tokens/{id}/revoke -> emits token.revoked event and invalidates introspection cache.

 dana: Observability ask: emit events for each priming request with fields: token_id, lease_id, region, step=(metadata|secret), size_estimate, operator_id. Link logs to these events.

ops-bot: infra-bot: created SLO dashboard stub: "hand-off priming failures" with alert threshold at 0.2%

ben: Security: no token should permit KMS decrypt. Token must be explicit about whether it allows secret-hydration. If secret-hydration allowed, require a separate KMS access grant with customer-managed key authorization.

priya: For secret-hydration we should surface two options: (A) delegated key access in target region (requires customer opt-in), (B) encrypted blob replication + rewrap in target region by customer KMS. Option B avoids us decrypting across regions. Document both in RFC.

marco: Implementation notes: lease-manager to mint tokens; auth-service to do introspection; dataplane to call auth-service on incoming X-Prewarm-Token. We'll use rotated signing key for tokens; keep introspection cache for 30s to avoid rate spike.

alice: Runbook item: if prewarm fails because secret-hydration blocked, control-plane should revert to prewarm-only mode and mark commit blocked with clear operator error and remediation steps.

ben: Add chaos scenario: simulate ephemeral network partition where token introspection fails. In that case, dataplane should fail closed for secret-steps and allow metadata-step if dry-token validated locally (cached).

priya: Edge-case: token replay across regions. We must include "issued_for_region" claim and validate matches X-Target-Region header. Reject if mismatch.

marco: QA plan: run small canary across 10 non-PII tenants, collect metrics: token-success-rate, secret-hydration-failure-rate, time-to-complete-priming.

dana: I'll prototype the dry-run UI and the CSV export. Also add a checkbox for "require compliance sign-off" which toggles commit blocked by default.

alice: Actions: 1) Priya write KMS patterns and consent schema; 2) Marco prototype token mint + introspection; 3) Ben add observability events + runbook; 4) Dana mock UI; 5) Alice to author short RFC extension that covers dry-run, token shapes, headers, and runbook.

ben: One more thing: add a metric for "potentially-sensitive items discovered during dry-run" so product can estimate migration effort.

priya: And include error codes in RFC: 403 CONSENT_REQUIRED, 410 TOKEN_EXPIRED, 409 TOKEN_REPLAY, 423 SECRET_HYDRATION_BLOCKED.

marco: I'll open branch `prototype/handoff-dryrun` and push a README with token schemas.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled staging job: handoff-dryrun-canary at 2026-04-06T02:00Z

alice: Thanks team. If we get this right, operator-driven cutovers will be auditable and safe for residency-bound customers.

ben: Agreed. Let's keep initial rollout conservative.

alice: RFC owners assigned. Closing thread for now; follow-ups in RFC PR.
